guide_property_purchase.title: Buying Property in Spain
guide_property_purchase.description: The comprehensive guide to buying property in Spain – from financing to getting the keys.

card.title: Buying Property in Spain
card.description: Comprehensive guide to property purchase: financing, purchase process, taxes and key players

hero.title: Buying Property in Spain – The Comprehensive Guide
hero.description: Buying a property in Spain is a dream for many. Sun, beach, your own home – whether as a vacation home, retirement investment, or permanent residence. But those who only know the purchase process from Germany will quickly realize: In Spain, many things work differently.

introduction.title: Introduction: Differences from Germany, what to expect
introduction.description: While the notary in Germany handles almost the entire legal review, their role in Spain is much more limited. Pre-contracts, down payments, and certain taxes are common here and can seem unfamiliar to German buyers. Those who are prepared and adjust to these differences can save themselves a lot of stress and ultimately receive the keys to their new apartment or house with peace of mind.

preparation_financing.title: Preparation & Financing
preparation_financing.description: Before things get concrete, you should realistically assess your finances.

equity.title: Equity
equity.description: Spanish banks typically finance only about 60–70% of the purchase price. You should therefore bring at least 30% yourself.

additional_costs.title: Additional Costs
additional_costs.description: Plan for an additional 10–15% of the purchase price. This includes taxes, notary and registry costs, as well as Gestoría fees.

mortgage.title: Mortgage
mortgage.description: Financing through German banks is difficult, as they usually don't register mortgages on Spanish properties. The usual route is therefore through a Spanish bank. There you get loans with fixed, variable, or mixed interest rates, often with terms up to 30 years.

requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.description: Banks require salary certificates or proof of income. As a foreigner without income in Spain, a higher equity ratio is often required.

reservation.title: Reservation ("reserva")
reservation.description: Often the process begins with a reservation: With a small sum (e.g., 1–2% of the purchase price), the property is taken off the market for you. This agreement is more informal but already binding.

pre_contract.title: Pre-contract ("contrato de arras")
pre_contract.description: The heart of the Spanish purchase process is the pre-contract. Here you typically pay 10% of the purchase price.
pre_contract.buyer_withdrawal: If the buyer withdraws, the down payment is forfeited.
pre_contract.seller_withdrawal: If the seller withdraws, they must pay back double the amount.
pre_contract.security: This gives you strong security that the property is really reserved for you.

main_contract.title: Main Contract at the Notary
main_contract.description: The final purchase contract ("escritura de compraventa") is signed at the notary. You bring the remaining amount – usually by bank check. The notary checks identity, basic documents, and notarizes the purchase. Unlike in Germany, however, they don't provide comprehensive legal advice.

registration.title: Registration in the Land Registry
registration.description: After signing at the notary, the property is registered in the land registry ("Registro de la Propiedad"). Only with this registration are you officially the owner. At the same time, the cadastre ("Catastro") is updated, which records area and building data.

notary.title: Notary
notary.description: Notarizes the purchase, checks formalities, but no deep legal review.

gestoria.title: Gestoría
gestoria.description: Highly recommended. They handle administrative procedures, tax payments, land registry entries, and utility registrations.

registro.title: Registro de la Propiedad
registro.description: The land registry office, where you are registered as the owner.

catastro.title: Catastro
catastro.description: Maintains location data, living area, property boundaries – important, as there are sometimes discrepancies with the land registry.

bank.title: Bank
bank.description: Essential for mortgage, payment processing, and bank checks.

taxes_costs.title: Taxes & Purchase Costs
taxes_costs.description: In addition to the purchase price, several costs come your way in Spain:

itp.title: ITP (Impuesto de Transmisiones Patrimoniales)
itp.description: Property transfer tax for used properties, 6–10% depending on the region.

iva.title: IVA (Value Added Tax)
iva.description: For new builds instead of ITP, currently 10%.

ajd.title: AJD (Actos Jurídicos Documentados)
ajd.description: Stamp tax on notarial documents, usually about 1%.

notary_register.title: Notary and Registry Costs
notary_register.description: Vary according to purchase price, together roughly 0.5–1.5%.

plusvalia.title: Plusvalía Municipal
plusvalia.description: Municipal tax on land value increase, normally paid by the seller – but clearly regulate this in the contract!

illegal_buildings.title: Illegal Buildings
illegal_buildings.description: Some extensions, pools, or roof terraces are not approved. Without a building permit (Licencia de Obra), high back payments or even demolitions can threaten.

outstanding_debts.title: Outstanding Debts
outstanding_debts.description: In Spain, community costs (Comunidad), property tax (IBI), or utility bills "attach" to the property. Always demand proof before purchase that no outstanding debts exist.

habitability_certificate.title: Missing Habitability Certificate
habitability_certificate.description: Without this certificate ("cédula de habitabilidad"), there can be problems with utilities.

mortgages_registry.title: Mortgages in the Land Registry
mortgages_registry.description: Make sure no old mortgage is still registered, or that it is deleted upon purchase.

after_purchase.title: After Purchase
after_purchase.description: The purchase is not yet complete with the signature at the notary. After that you must:

steps.registry: have the property registered in the land registry
steps.utilities: transfer water, electricity, gas, and internet
steps.non_resident_tax: possibly pay the non-resident tax (Modelo 210), if you don't live permanently in Spain

after_purchase.gestoria_recommendation: A Gestoría takes care of all these steps for a fee – highly recommended if you're not on site or want to save time.

tips.nie_number: Get NIE number: Nothing works without it. Take care of this early.
tips.bank_account: Open Spanish bank account: Essential for purchase price, taxes, and additional costs.
tips.debt_certificates: Request debt-free certificates: Both from the land registry and the homeowners' association.
tips.read_contracts: Read Reserva & Arras carefully: These contracts are legally binding – much is decided here.
tips.plan_buffer: Plan enough buffer: Not only financially, but also time-wise. Some registrations or administrative procedures take weeks.
tips.use_professionals: Involve professionals: A good real estate agent, a reliable Gestoría, and possibly a lawyer will save you many problems.

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.description: Buying a property in Spain is an exciting project – but not a walk in the park. With good preparation, sufficient equity, and the right professionals by your side, however, the process runs smoothly. It's important to know the differences from Germany: down payments, different contract forms, and additional taxes.
conclusion.final_thought: If you keep these things in mind and don't let yourself be rushed, you can safely realize your dream of your own house or apartment in Spain. And then only the best remains: moving in, enjoying the terrace, and beginning your new life in Spain.
